copy.blurb:
The model fancies Qatar more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Switzerland. +11.9pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

Elo numbers going in: Qatar 1640, Switzerland 1830. That's a 190-point lead for Switzerland — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Qatar to win at 20%, the draw at 19%, and Switzerland to win at 61%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Qatar sits at 20% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Qatar to win at 8%, the draw at 16%, and Switzerland to win at 76%. On the Qatar side specifically the market reads 8%, which prices out at American odds of +1076. Compared against the model's 20%, that's the +11.9pp gap the Pick rests on.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Qatar, that haircut lands the model at 15%; the market is at 8%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.4pp. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Qatar side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 25 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +11.9pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Qatar are mispriced. Our number reads 20% on the home side; the market reads 8%. The +11.9pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Qatar v Switzerland · the model leans Qatar
